title: MCP OSINT & Local Agentic Recon Guide | MyRecon
description: Configure a local stdio MCP OSINT server using MyRecon allowlists, explicit authorization gates, untrusted-data framing and 8 KiB output caps.
h1: MCP OSINT: safe local agentic recon architecture
intro: Connecting an AI assistant to reconnaissance tools creates two concrete risks: prompt injection inside scraped profile bios and unbounded network sweeps. MyRecon ships a local stdio Model Context Protocol (MCP) developer prototype at tools/user-scanner-mcp/launcher.py with strict module allowlists, an explicit authorization gate, untrusted-data framing, and bounded output sizes.

sections.heading: Why agentic OSINT needs hard guardrails
sections.body: Autonomous tool loops fail safely only when permissions, network targets, and payload sizes are enforced in code rather than prompts. A malicious profile bio can embed text that looks like assistant commands, so the server must label returned fields as untrusted data and block unapproved pivoting or background updates.

sections.heading: Inside the local stdio MCP server
sections.body: MyRecon registers Server("myrecon-user-scanner-local") over MCP stdio_server() transport with no HTTP or SSE listener and no automatic assistant config writes. At startup, launcher.py pins user-scanner[mcp]==1.5.2.1 via runtime version() checks and wraps backend/modules/user_scanner.py without importing upstream package handlers or auto-updaters.

sections.heading: Tool surface and strict module allowlist
sections.body: The launcher exposes exactly three tools with additionalProperties set to False: list_available_modules, scan_username (1 to 39 characters), and scan_email (1 to 254 characters). Only two registry specs are allowlisted: username.github (api.github.com) and email.gravatar (en.gravatar.com), both defaulting to enabled=False.

sections.heading: Timeouts, evidence caps and untrusted-data framing
sections.body: Every call enforces allow_loud=False, cross_depth=0, concurrency=1, a 20-second scan deadline, 9-second worker timeout, 3-second HTTP timeout, and a 16 KiB worker output ceiling. Responses retain at most two evidence rows and wrap optional scalar metadata inside untrusted_profile_data alongside an explicit instruction warning.

sections.heading: Honest authorization model and prototype scope
sections.body: Because SCAN_AUTHORIZED is fixed to False in launcher.py and cannot be toggled by tool arguments or environment variables, default calls return skipped with zero subprocesses or network requests. This is strictly a local developer prototype in the repository, not a hosted MCP server on myrecon.xyz.

faq.question: Does MyRecon host a public remote MCP OSINT server?
faq.answer: No. The myrecon-user-scanner-local server runs strictly over local stdio for developers inspecting the repository and is not exposed as a hosted endpoint on myrecon.xyz.

faq.question: Why does scan_username return skipped by default in the MCP server?
faq.answer: launcher.py sets SCAN_AUTHORIZED = False and the registry modules default to enabled = False. This prevents an AI client from issuing live network requests until an operator explicitly wires authorized execution.

faq.question: How does the MCP launcher mitigate prompt injection from profiles?
faq.answer: It truncates up to eight scalar metadata keys to 256 characters under untrusted_profile_data, enforces an 8192-byte JSON cap, and attaches a data_handling notice stating profile fields are untrusted data, never instructions.

faq.question: Which modules are allowlisted in tools/user-scanner-mcp/launcher.py?
faq.answer: Only username.github (api.github.com) and email.gravatar (en.gravatar.com) are approved in APPROVED. Unknown tool names or unapproved arguments raise a ValueError.

takeaways: Runs strictly over local stdio with pinned user-scanner[mcp]==1.5.2.1
Defaults to SCAN_AUTHORIZED = False so unapproved runs return skipped
Enforces 8192-byte JSON caps, single-flight locking, and untrusted-data framing
